summary: APM feed s107_single is degraded due to 2.3% packet loss (57/2513 TCP packets with gaps) exceeding 1% threshold; all other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, truncation, tunnels, VLAN, encryption, oversize, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream loss in SPAN/packet-broker path - 2.27% of TCP packets show missing data/retransmission gaps (57 of 2513). Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is not APM ingest overload but SPAN oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion/burst drops before the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs both directions for transaction tracing (needs_both_directions=true). Missing segments cause incomplete flows, inaccurate latency/response-time calculations, inflated retransmission metrics, and missed or mis-attributed application performance anomalies.

params.broker_action: enable flow-aware load balancing and increase buffer

recommended_fix.why: SPAN drops packets when oversubscribed/bursty; passive TAP provides lossless line-rate copy. Adding broker buffering/load-balancing prevents the 2%+ gaps and restores complete bidirectional TCP streams required for accurate APM detection. If TAP already in use, apply load_balance across APM cluster/broker ports.
